Where it began

Wriddhiman Saha was born in Siliguri on 24 October 1984, and studied at Siliguri College of Commerce. He came through Bengal's Under-19 and Under-22 sides, and when his first-class debut finally came, against Hyderabad in the Ranji Trophy of 2007–08, he marked it with 111 not out.

That hundred opened doors quickly. The Kolkata Knight Riders signed him for the first season of the Indian Premier League in 2008.

The player

His Test debut was one of the oddest on record. He was in the squad against South Africa in February 2010 as the reserve keeper, with no expectation of playing, but one batsman was not fit and the only spare batsman was hurt in a kickabout before play on the opening day. With nobody else to hand, India picked their reserve gloveman as a batsman. He made 36 in the second innings.

For several years his chances came mostly when MS Dhoni was unavailable. In 2016 he toured the West Indies as India's keeper, and over the following seasons he was behind the stumps for many of their Tests. He played 40 Tests between 2010 and 2021, scoring 1,353 runs at 29.41 with three hundreds, and took 92 catches and 12 stumpings. His best innings was 117 against Australia at the JSCA International Stadium in 2017, when he and Cheteshwar Pujara added 199 for the seventh wicket.

What made him special

His keeping was the heart of it, and he had a gift for the catch that looked out of reach. In 2018 against South Africa he became the first Indian keeper to hold ten catches in a Test, and in 2019 he became only the fifth Indian keeper to reach 100 Test dismissals.

With the bat he was steady rather than spectacular in Tests, though he could hit very hard when the mood took him. In 2018 he made a hundred from just 20 balls in a domestic match, a record.

Away from the middle

In the 2014 IPL final he became the first man to make a hundred in an IPL final, an unbeaten 115 from 55 balls for Kings XI Punjab. He went on to play for the Chennai Super Kings, the Sunrisers Hyderabad and the Gujarat Titans. He finished where he started, with Bengal, playing his last match in the Ranji Trophy in February 2025, which Bengal won by an innings.

And finally

Few players have been told they were playing a Test for reasons quite so unexpected as a game of football in the warm-up. He spent the next decade proving the selectors had stumbled on something good.
